news_summary: Energy Transfer posted a large Q2 2026 earnings and EBITDA beat on Aug 4, 2026, driven by data-center and power-generation natural-gas demand, and raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8B-$19.1B (from $18.2B-$18.6B). Alongside earnings the partnership announced its 19th consecutive quarterly distribution increase to $0.34/unit and, in June 2026, a fully-subscribed expansion of its Nederland NGL export terminal with ethane volumes contracted into the 2040s. Separately, Shell and Phillips 66 are reportedly exploring a sale of their combined Explorer Pipeline stake (~$3.5B valuation); Energy Transfer holds a minority stake and could potentially join a sale, though no deal is confirmed.

catalysts.what: Energy Transfer reported Q2 2026 results: EPS $0.59 (vs ~$0.37-$0.38 consensus), adjusted EBITDA $5.07B (+31% YoY from $3.87B), distributable cash flow to partners +32% YoY to $2.59B. Raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8B-$19.1B from $18.2B-$18.6B, citing growing data-center and power-generation gas demand.

Energy Transfer announced its 19th consecutive quarterly distribution increase, to $0.34 per common unit ($1.36 annualized, up more than 3% YoY), payable Aug 19, 2026 to unitholders of record as of Aug 7, 2026.

Energy Transfer announced a fully-subscribed expansion of its Nederland NGL export terminal (Port Neches, TX): +240,000 bpd ethane and +55,000 bpd LPG export capacity, with 100% of the added ethane capacity committed under long-term contracts running into the 2040s; staged in-service beginning 2028, with additional ship docks completing mid-2029.

Shell and Phillips 66 are reportedly weighing a sale of their combined ~61% stake in the Explorer refined-products pipeline (~$3.5B valuation), with Greenhill and RBC Capital Markets retained to run an auction. Energy Transfer and MPLX hold the remaining stake and could potentially contribute their holdings if buyer interest is strong; sources caution the process is early-stage with no guarantee of a deal.

move_thesis: ET has been moving on data-center and power-generation-driven natural gas demand flowing directly into results: the large Q2 EPS/EBITDA beat and a further full-year EBITDA guidance raise (the second raise so far in 2026, per prior guidance updates referenced in coverage) reflect that trend, reinforced by a 19th consecutive quarterly distribution increase and a fully-subscribed, multi-decade-contracted Nederland NGL export expansion that locks in ethane demand growth. A speculative near-term catalyst is the reported Shell/Phillips 66 exploration of a sale of Explorer Pipeline stakes, in which ET holds a minority interest and could potentially participate -- unconfirmed and described as early-stage as of late July 2026.
